scenes.say: Ever wondered how Kafka lets you scale reading huge streams of data? Why do consumer groups matter so much?

scenes.label: Group
scenes.sub: A consumer group splits the work of reading a topic.
scenes.say: A consumer group is a set of consumers sharing the load. Each partition goes to one consumer in the group.
Kafka splits topics into partitions. Each partition is assigned to a consumer. That means parallel reads, boosting throughput.

scenes.title: Tracking Progress
scenes.say: Consumers track their progress using offsets. This lets them resume from where they left off after a restart.

scenes.question: What happens if a consumer leaves?
scenes.right: Kafka triggers a rebalance. Partitions are reassigned, so no data is lost.
scenes.say: If a consumer leaves, Kafka triggers a rebalance. Partitions are reassigned so data keeps flowing, but you might see a brief pause.
